source.quote: Greetings, travelers, and welcome back to Goldbound. Our rogue, Goldilock, is still locked within the borders of Ellen Forest. He can't leave, not until he earns enough gold to buy a WoW token. Only then can he pay the gold toll and unlock the next chapter of his journey, a neighboring zone. Now, there are a few ground rules to keep Goldilock honest. First off, he's solo self-found, which means every item must be gathered, looted, quested, or bought from vendors within unlocked zones. Stormwood counts, but primarily for banking and auction house access. So, we can sell to other players, but we can't buy. No trades, no shortcuts. This raw effort turned into raw gold. And the price of freedom being a WOW token that varies with the market from day to day. Not only is the Wow token price up, but so is the supply of every single item Goldilock has been farming. On our last swing through Mother Fang's cave, we weren't alone. A whole crew of travelers were already camped out. Some looked a little familiar. Uh, okay. Now, don't get me wrong, I love seeing people take on this challenge, but I'll be honest, it's getting a little crowded in Elwin.

source.quote: So, I started mapping, looking for a loop with minimal filler, no fur, no fangs, just leather. And what I found was amazing. You see, down south in Ellwin is a small and unassuming vineyard, Mccclure Vineyard. Grapes, sure, but more importantly, bores. Roughly eight spawn around the farm. But here's where it gets interesting. You see, they're tied to a quest, which means they're hyper spawncoded. If you're not familiar with hyperspawns, here's the breakdown. As long as players are killing them, the game forces at least one or two to always be alive. So, no matter how fast you clear them, they keep on coming. And because the vineyard is tight in a small area, it's the perfect live towin grind spot. Now, the only thing left is to leverage my extensive macro riding experience from my totally legitimate Challenger Arena titles. And I built a bore aimbot. So, basically, this is a onebutton bore killing machine. It casts my range abilities, pops my movement speed cool downs, pops my damage cool downs on repeat. So, I just walk in circles pressing this key and the boores die on repeat. Here's how you run this farm properly. You don't loot. Seriously, just kill them on repeat for 3 to 4 minutes straight. No looting, no skinning, just bore after boar and they'll start stacking up. A nice satisfying bore pile. Then, once the ground is properly cursed, then you loot. You skin them all in one go and it's just way faster with less downtime.

source.quote: Well, they only cost three light leather per craft. And if you compare that to the five, six, or eight of some other green armor pieces, it's a lower input to get to a disenchantable item. So, we'll get better margins because we're not crafting the gear. We're crafting for a disenchant shuffle. And I'll be honest, this is where the shuffle took a turn. You see, I had a plan. I was going to use the leatherworking modifier relics of the past to scale these gloves in level. I thought maybe, just maybe, I could squeeze out higher level greens using nothing but element mats and then disenchant those scaled greens for better and better enchanting materials. So, I guess we'll have to wait to see if the shuffle really pays off when I unlock a new trade goods vendor that has the curing salt. I mean, we've still got the greens, so we can swap over to enchanting on some basic disenchanting. source.quote: But hey, just because Goldilock is stuck in the past farming low-level mobs for vendor trash doesn't mean you have to be. So whether you're playing retail classic, Season Discovery, or Kata, if you want to actually enjoy making gold and make a lot of it, maybe even earn a WoW token or two, then check out Goldcap. They've got hundreds of guides for every version of the game, plus access to premium Discords full of other content creators and master farmers who can point you in the right direction. some that don't spend all their days skinning hyperspawn bores. Membership gets you access, but they also have individual guides if you're interested. So, I'll drop a link below and use code path 10 to save 10% and help support the channel. All right, Goldilock is back at it. After developing the element shuffle in episodes 1 and two, and discovering that yes, you can actually mine ore while mounted, but not herbs, I started thinking. Is dual gathering really worth it? Or would I make more gold per hour just mining non-stop? So, today we're putting it to the test. Three runs, 1 hour each. First up, mining only. We'll be able to stay mounted for this entire run, and I'm thinking it might be pretty efficient. Second, we're going to be doing dual gathering, our classic mining and herbalism gathering method. And third, just to make sure we're being exhaustive, we're going to do herbalism only. We're keeping it simple. And for the calculations, I am going to process these with the L and shuffle, but we're going to exclude the processing time for the ores and herbs because frankly, the herbs process so fast and I just smelt the bars and make the copper bullets while cooking dinner or vacuuming or maybe even watching some YouTube. So, let's get into it. First up, 1 hour of mining only. And from mining only, we walked away with 631 copper ore, as well as 15 gems. Now, at a pre-shuffle rate of about 4 gold, 50 silver per ore, that's 2,839 gold straight up. But once we smelt it all down and convert to copper bolts, so we bump our total final value to about 4,600 gold for the hour. That's pretty respectable for a starting zone.
